main_text.l: Neutra in al aut ar definentia: ut Vectigal, sol[?] ab
hoc vectigali. Calcar,
ein spor[?] ab hoc calcari. Præter, Sal, salʒ. Hepar, Die Läber. Far[?] Jubar, der
schein vnd glantz eines feurigen dinges. Nectar, ein
süß tranck der Heydnischen Götter: quæ e habent:
ut, fale, hepate, farre, jubare, nectare.
Adjectiva unius terminationis e vel i habent: ut,
amans, ab hoc amante vel amanti. Degener, degene-
re vel degeneri. Excipe, pauper, sopes[?] & alia nonnul-
la. Item & Comparativi e vel i habent: ut, Major, ma-
jore, vel majori.

l.i: Quæ habent in Nominativo plurali ia?

main_text.l: Neutra, quorum Ablativus singularis in i tantum,
vel in e & i simul definit: ut, ab hoc vectigali, hæc ve-
ctigalia: ab hoc audace vel audaci, hæc audacia. Ex-
cipe, Vetus, vetera: Et Comparativos: ut Majora, plura
Veteres plura & pluria dixere.

l.i: Quæ habent in Genitivo plurali ium?

main_text.l: Nomina, quorum Ablativus singularis in i tatum,
vel in e & i simul exit: ut, ab hoc animali horum ani-
malium. Ab hoc, hac,
hoc fœlice, vel fœlici, horum,
harum, horum fœlicium. Deinde ium habent, quo-
rum Nominativus singularis in duas consonas exit:
ut, pars, partium, ein theil. Falx, falciu, ein sichel/ oder
Trum[?] schneidmesser. Merx, mercium, Kauffmans
wahr/ oder gut. Sapiens, sapientium vel sapientum,
weisse. Parens, parentium vel parentum, die eltern.
Tertio monosyllaba quædam: ut, Cor, cordium. Lis,
litium. Mas, marium. Mus, murium. Os, ossium.
Primo, Comparativi: ut, Major, majorum. Melior,
meliorum. Plus habet plurium. Deinde hæc sequentia:

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the German glosses after "Vectigal" (sol[?]), "Calcar" (spor[?]), "Far[?]" and "Trum[?]" are hard to read at this scan quality. "sopes[?]" is read as one word. The heading "plurali ia?" and the page number "73[?]" are uncertain. The gloss "Tertio monosyllaba" line and the "ium" forms follow the printed order. The Latin "fale" is copied as printed. No catchword, footnote or running-text cont marker is visible.
